sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Deepak Soni - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri B.K. Upadhyay - Government Advocate for the respond  ORDER

This is the third application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 r/w Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on behalf of applicant, who is in jail since 10.12.2021 in relation to FIR/Crime No.411/2021, registered at Police Station Laur, District Rewa, for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 of IPC and Section 66-D of Information Technology Act.

2. Counsel for the applicant submits that the present bail application has been filed on the ground of delay in trial as witnesses, despite calling by the Court time and again, are not coming towards the Court for recording their statement.
However, it is submitted that on 27.02.2025, this Court has called the status report of the trial.

It is submitted that the applicant is in jail since 10.12.2021 and under the existing scenario, it is not sure as to when the trial would be concluded and looking to the applicant's custody period, he may be enlarged on bail.

3. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that looking to the nature of offence committed by the applicant, he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

It is further submitted that mere NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12735 2 Pushpendra Yadav Alias Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2474831/
1 MCRC-7251-2025 delay in trial would not entitle the applicant to be enlarged on bail.

entities.text: Pushpendra Yadav Alias Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of case diary especially the status report dated 07.03.2025, I am of the opinion that the reasons assigned by the Court for causing delay in trial and explanation submitted in that regard do not appear to be cogent and sufficient.
The bail application, therefore, is being considered only on the ground of delay in trial.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

5. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned.
6. On being released on bail, the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 480(3) of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7. However, it is expected that the trial Court shall expedite the trial and make all possible efforts to conclude it at the earliest.

If the witnesses are not coming to the Court for recording their statement,
then the Court would be at liberty to adopt coercive steps to secure their presence before it.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Rao Pushpendra Yadav Alias Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2474831/
